inventory.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
inventory.visualPurpose: The dedicated Atropine block's own printed set (the section's sole visual element — the ORGAN SYSTEM/ACTION/NOTES grid with its NOTES cell, plus the ADVERSE EFFECTS tier: findings cell, cautions line, the seven-line mnemonic, and the Jimson weed line)
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: ONE THREE-COLUMN TEXT TABLE + ADVERSE-EFFECTS TIER (PURE TEXT — ZERO rasters on pdf 262-263; pdfimages returns no rows; COPYRIGHTED, never reproduced as artwork). Intro: 'Muscarinic antagonist. Used to treat bradycardia and for ophthalmic applications.' Column headers: ORGAN SYSTEM / ACTION / NOTES. Six rows: 'Eye' → '↑ pupil dilation, cycloplegia'; 'Airway' → 'Bronchodilation, ↓ secretions'; 'Heart' → '↑ heart rate'; 'Stomach' → '↓ acid secretion'; 'Gut' → '↓ motility'; 'Bladder' → '↓ urgency in cystitis'; printed NOTES cell: 'Blocks muscarinic effects (DUMBBELSS) of anticholinesterases, but not the nicotinic effects'. ADVERSE EFFECTS tier: '↑ body temperature (due to ↓ sweating); ↑ HR; dry mouth; dry, flushed skin; cycloplegia; constipation; disorientation' + 'Can cause acute angle-closure glaucoma in older adults (due to mydriasis), urinary retention in men with prostatic hyperplasia, and hyperthermia in infants' + the book's OWN seven-line mnemonic under its printed label 'Adverse effects:' ('Hot as a hare / Fast as a fiddle / Dry as a bone / Red as a beet / Blind as a bat / Mad as a hatter / Full as a flask') + 'Jimson weed (Datura) → gardener's pupil (mydriasis)'. Carried VERBATIM as the note's two table blocks and conveyed as ONE original KYP toxicity map (the six-lane action grid, the simile-to-arrow mapping band, the antidote-mirror strip, the Jimson weed card, the boundary strip, the reading-rule footer) — no artwork reproduced.
